text: Plasma Proteomic Signatures Predict Incident Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis: A Prospective Study Stratified by C9orf72 Expansion. Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a progressive and fatal neurological disorder for which reliable preclinical biomarkers to predict disease onset are currently lacking. Plasma proteomics offers a promising avenue for early detection. The identification of plasma proteins and pathways associated with incident ALS holds potential to improve early diagnosis, enable risk stratification and provide insights into disease mechanisms.

Metabolic traits and adaptations of mice lacking Slc12a5 in insulin-secreting β-cells. Pancreatic β-cells integrate metabolic and electrical signals to couple nutrient sensing with insulin secretion, yet the physiological contribution of the neuronal K+Cl- cotransporter-2, Kcc2 (Slc12a5) to β-cell function and whole-body metabolic regulation remains incompletely understood. To define its role in vivo, we generated mice lacking Kcc2 selectively in insulin-secreting β-cells (Kcc2βKO) and evaluated growth, body composition, feeding behavior, glucose homeostasis and islet function from weaning through early adulthood. Kcc2βKO mice developed sex- and age-dependent metabolic phenotypes. Females exhibited lower body weight at weaning and increased lean mass during adulthood, whereas males displayed reduced body-weight gain despite increased food intake. Feeding microstructure analyses identified age-dependent alterations in meal patterning in male Kcc2βKO mice. Morphometric analysis demonstrated increased mean islet area without changes in endocrine cell composition, and isolated islets exhibited enhanced glucose-stimulated insulin secretion at younger ages. Male, but not female, Kcc2βKO mice showed improved glucose tolerance and age-dependent differences in glycemic responses to exogenous insulin, whereas both sexes exhibited attenuated glycemic responses to alanine challenge. Fasting blood glucose remained largely preserved across genotypes, although fasting plasma insulin concentrations varied according to sex, age and fasting duration. These findings identify β-cell Kcc2 as a physiological contributor to nutrient-stimulated insulin secretion and demonstrate that disruption of β-cell chloride homeostasis is accompanied by integrated, age- and sex-dependent adaptations in body-weight regulation, feeding behavior and glucose homeostasis.

Associations between dietary scores and metabolic health in later reproductive years: results from the ROLO longitudinal study. Cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of death in women globally. Healthy dietary patterns are associated with favourable metabolic health profiles in women; however, most studies focus on the reproductive years or post menopause. This research aimed to explore associations between dietary scores and cardiometabolic health in women in later reproductive years.
